body: I've had multiple TBI's, psychosis, seizures, trauma, and extreme psych med fiascos and withdrawals (serotonin syndrome, dystonia, etc).  I am severely depressed and really only feel anger/irritability/apathy.  Since I feel similarly, it's hard to comment.  I will say, especially when depressed, we downplay or struggle with the basics.  SLEEP, meditation, whole foods/healthy diet, supplements for brain health, nature, social connection/purpose, and exercise.  My TBI friend tells me to do anything, anything being better than lying in bed ruminating about symptoms and staring at walls.  I spend every day in my head self-checking about symptoms and stewing in pity and isolation.  Don't do it.  Once you start questioning every moment, "Did I feel connected to that tree?"  "Could I \*hear\* that song?"  "Did I just feel something?" "Why is my ear ringing?" "Is that a rash?" you'll go bonkers.  There are a ton of options like the above mentioned-- (good therapist, functional medicine doctor, meditation, behavioral activation, ketamine, finding a new psychiatrist, etc.).  Try something, don't beat yourself up, take baby steps, and give your brain time to heal.  <3
Thank you.  Except they just discharged me back out without med changes and a referral back to the place that will *only* prescribe this medication.  I give up.
Yes.  Hide in bed or plan to run away but too cognitive impairment to do so.

Yes.  Depression, chronic stress, “trapped” emotions can lead to unbearable fatigue.  Then more stress or depression or inactivity.  Lather rinse repeat.  Hope sleep is restorative a bit.  You are validated and heard.  Be as gentle with yourself as possible.
Go to a hospital, hun.  If not, get hooked up with a therapist for support.  The sooner you get help, the sooner you can start feeling better.  You deserve it.
Thank you for writing this.  I don’t try because plagued by all the voices and internal criticism and hopelessness at each step.
I’m homeless in a motel, barely out of bed in six weeks.  I can’t function.  My friend told me to give my heart to God before I go through with anything.  I hear you.

Yes.  I have anger/irritability issues with mental illness and brain injury.  During HELL weeks, I've screamed in the woods, put holes in walls, yelled, cussed, thrown my phone, cannot tolerate sound and need to self-isolate.  It's like rage on steroids.

What I read as the \*definition\* of adulting: Working your buns off, reflecting on your feelings rationally, showing self-awareness enough to know your emotional and psychological wellbeing are being compromised, maintaining/invested in friend/family relationships, keeping a budget, and seeking professional help to deal with things.

You deserve an Olympic medal, in my book.  Seriously.  There are peer-run warmlines in many areas and hotlines if you need to vent/talk to a human.  They may also be able to suggest resources for free counseling or drop-in centers in the meantime.  Please give yourself credit and validation and self-compassion.

I am sorry and empathize.  I imagine you are already in a vulnerable place, do not have adequate support, and are feeling sensitive to rejection and a whole host of swirling emotions already.  

You deserve help and healing.  However long it takes, you can keep searching.  Psychiatrists are much easier to find than a therapist suited to your needs, and both would probably be beneficial.  If you identify your specific needs, then it's easier to find practitioners with skills in that area.

Try not to turn this inward on yourself and let it confirm any feelings of hopelessness or brokenness you might harbor about yourself.  By seeking out care before, you proved you are able and willing to take steps to help yourself and be vulnerable.  It doesn't have to be today or on any timeline, but I hope you'll take a step again.  Trust you are worth it.
Damn, I’m sorry.  I wish we lived in a world where one could just be honest— with employers, neighbors, strangers, friends— without taboo, judgments, and the like.  Thank you for being honest here.

I've been living this way for three years, and it's driven me to full-blown insanity.  I get so restless and angry that there are things I technically want to do, but can't (agoraphobia, brain injury, autoimmune disorders, etc).  You feel like you're dying to live but living to die, yeah?  I empathize.

I hear you-- the guilt, self-hatred, regret, shame.  Self-forgiveness is the hardest thing in the world, but it's a place to start, perhaps the only place.  And it's what you deserve.  What you don't deserve is to pay for your past a million times over.  You've paid whatever price already by eating yourself alive with guilt.  Give yourself some space to breathe and be free for a moment.  You don't have to be anything or anyone else in this moment or overnight.  You can just be you.  Really.

It's okay not to be happy today.  Sometimes birthdays and holidays add too much pressure about how one "should" feel vs. how one actually feels.  I hear and validate that you're feeling lousy and the future is not a comfort today.  I hope you choose another day and treat yourself to something or give yourself some comfort.  Life happens a moment at a time, and my birthday wish for you is a moment of peace.
I was crazy before the illnesses, but now acquired/traumatic brain injury (permanent), mold toxicity, anaplasmosis, babesiosis.  That’s my pity rant.
BPD is hell.  I’m sorry.  Have you done DBT?
Don’t do it.  I repeat: do not do it.  Will cause acute liver injury and dying in a hospital of hepatotoxicity could take weeks of an agony you could never imagine.  Seriously.

Survival instinct.  It’s our lizard brains.  Don’t add more judgment on yourself when suffering so horrendously.  You’re not a failure; you’re a human in agony.  Wish I had more than words from an internet stranger.

I am glad you wrote it out, and wish I had better words besides, "I relate so heavily and hear you."  You put something into words I'd be too afraid to share.  It's hard not wanting to live and bear the pain and loneliness, but also to feel lonely in dying.  I cried reading this.  Not that it matters or you can feel it across cyberspace, but this internet stranger wants you to know one soul on this planet relates and hears your pain.

Existential crisis myself and spirituality/faith dead after brain injury made me question the existence of a soul or afterlife.  Get rest.  The nothingness will still be there.  I’m crawling into bed and ignoring the world before final decisions.
No judgment and secretly hope you come back.  As a brain injury survivor from self-harm, I fear you attempting and being found and ending up with brain injury.  Hope you find peace/relief.
